subject: radiology
title: Obstetric, gynaecological and breast imaging: key high-yield facts

steps.tx: Early pregnancy ultrasound begins with the **gestational sac**, the first sign of an intrauterine pregnancy that becomes visible on transvaginal scanning. The **yolk sac** follows and helps confirm the pregnancy. **Fetal heart activity** is detected later. Transvaginal probes give better resolution than transabdominal probes, which is why they are preferred in the early weeks.

steps.tx: Gestational age is estimated by the **crown-rump length** in the first trimester, which is the most accurate method. Femur length and **biparietal diameter** are used in the second and third trimesters. Abdominal and head circumference are used in the third trimester, and abdominal circumference reflects size and weight more than age. Nuchal translucency is measured between 11 and 13 plus 6 weeks, with CRL between 45 and 84 mm.

steps.tx: **Nuchal translucency** is the most effective sonographic marker of trisomy 21 at 11 to 14 weeks. An NT below 3.5 mm is normal in this window. In the second trimester, a raised **nuchal skin fold** carries the highest risk for Down syndrome. Anomaly scan is done at 18 to 20 weeks, best at 20 weeks. Diagnosis of chromosomal disease is confirmed by karyotype from amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling.

steps.tx: Obstetric ultrasound signs of **spina bifida** include the **banana sign**, where the cerebellum wraps around the brainstem with obliteration of the cisterna magna, and the **lemon sign** of frontal bone flattening. Ventriculomegaly is also seen. Earliest detectable congenital anomaly on ultrasound is anencephaly, diagnosed from about 10 weeks and with full accuracy by 12 weeks. Placenta praevia is confirmed by locating the placenta over the os on ultrasound.
